artworks.title: Perithoos and Hippodameia
artworks.description: Attic red-figure volute-krater (British Museum F272): Peirithous leads Hippodameia as bride while Lapiths and Centaurs explode into the wedding fight. The vase names the Lapith queen at the hinge of the Centauromachy — civilization’s feast tipping into the battle that Ovid and the Parthenon metopes would retell for centuries.

artworks.title: The Battle of the Lapiths and Centaurs
artworks.description: Jordaens packs the Thessalian wedding into Baroque tumult: Centaurs seize women, Lapiths strike back, and Hippodameia’s nuptial peace is the wreck at the center. The Antwerp canvas is among the fullest early-modern images of the bride whose feast became the myth of civilized order under attack.

artworks.title: Combat of the Centaurs and the Lapiths
artworks.description: Bouguereau’s early Salon machine freezes bodies mid-struggle — a Centaur wrenching a Lapith woman while spears flash behind. Painted as academic proof of Ovid’s Metamorphoses XII, it keeps Hippodameia’s wedding as the French nineteenth century’s preferred arena for mythic violence and marble flesh.

artworks.title: The Abduction of Hippodamia
artworks.description: Bronze group (National Gallery of Art): a Centaur rears with Hippodameia locked against his chest — the single abduction that ignites the Lapith wedding. Carrier-Belleuse’s Second Empire drama, with Rodin’s contested hand in the modelling, is the sculpture that turned Peirithous’ bride into a portable storm of bronze and desire.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses XII (Centauromachy)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid’s Nestor tells how Eurytion seized Hippodameia at Peirithous’ feast — the Latin set-piece that made the Lapith bride the spark of the Centaur war.
